summary.oneLiner: Iykot Hitech Toolroom Limited is a small Chennai-based designer and manufacturer of moulds, dies, tools and plastic components that has pivoted into contract and component manufacturing of kitchen and home appliances under its own 'ZADASTAR' brand, and is now proposing a further diversification …
summary.business: The Company designs and manufactures moulds, dies, tools and plastic components and supplies mould components to other industries, operating from Chennai, Tamil Nadu. Following the introduction of its proprietary brand 'ZADASTAR', it transitioned into component and contract manufacturing of kitchen and home appliances for the domestic consumer durables market. Core toolroom operations consolidated during FY 2025-26 on lower business volumes and subdued demand, and management states it does not presently envisage significant opportunities in its existing business segments.

Home / kitchen appliances: Kitchen and home appliance components (contract manufacturing)
Proposed new vertical: Bullion and retail trading of gold, silver and other precious metals (subject to shareholder and regulatory approval)

currentContext.strategies: Diversify into the bullion and retail sector - trading and retail of gold, silver and other precious metals - as a revised business strategy, subject to shareholder approval and regulatory compliance; management states it does not presently envisage significant opportunities in its existing business segments.|Scale the domestic home/kitchen appliance vertical through component and contract manufacturing under the proprietary 'ZADASTAR' brand, leveraging scalable contract manufacturing opportunities in consumer durables.|Sustain promotion and marketing campaigns to build 'ZADASTAR' brand equity and expand the market footprint.|Complete the structural change following the Share Purchase Agreement and Open Offer by Aspect Global Ventures Private Limited, with a fresh board reconstitution and strategic redirection under the new leadership.|Stabilise operations post-promoter exit and clean up the capital structure - conversion of partly paid rights shares and forfeiture of the unpaid balance to leave only fully paid shares.|Organisational restructuring of the workforce to align with incoming promoter guidelines, alongside talent acquisition in product design and marketing, skill development for production staff, and performance-based incentives.|Conserve resources for ongoing operational transitions - no dividend recommended for FY 2025-26.
currentContext.expansion: The annual report discloses no capital-expenditure project, no plant addition and no capacity expansion with a commissioning or ramp timeline. What it describes instead is a business-model expansion: after introducing its proprietary brand 'ZADASTAR', the Company transitioned into component and contract manufacturing of kitchen and home appliances and sustained promotion and marketing campaigns through the year to build brand equity and expand its market footprint, which it calls a pivotal, ongoing shift in its product portfolio aimed at leveraging scalable contract manufacturing opportunities. Beyond that, management says it does not presently envisage significant opportunities in its existing business segments and proposes - subject to shareholder approval and regulatory compliance - to diversify into the bullion and retail sector, trading and retailing gold, silver and other precious metals, which it intends to scale under the new leadership following the Share Purchase Agreement and Open Offer by Aspect Global Ventures Private Limited. No site, investment amount, capacity or date is attached to either initiative. On funding, management flags that after the forfeiture of 99,01,931 partly paid-up equity shares on non-payment of final call money, 'managing liquid cash flows for expansions remains a key priority'.
currentContext.mdna: Management describes the outlook as 'transformative', driven by structural change following the SPA and Open Offer by Aspect Global Ventures Private Limited rather than by the existing business.|Consumer appliances - specifically kitchenware under contract and part-manufacturing setups - is said to offer consistent demand driven by household consumption.|The toolroom and industrial core moulding segment faces heightened cost pressures and competitive pricing; high-precision tooling remains critical, but manufacturers must optimise material costs and capacity utilisation to maintain margins.|Indian macro backdrop cited as supportive: resilient economy, projected GDP growth of approximately 7.4%-7.7% for FY26, government-led reforms, infrastructure spending and PLI-scheme incentives boosting manufacturing.|Core toolroom operations consolidated during the year on lower business volumes and subdued demand, with revenue described as dropping to approximately Rs.1.56 Crore from Rs.5.01 Crore in FY24-25.|Management points to sequential improvement, reporting a profit before tax in Q4 FY 2025-26 after losses in the first three quarters, and says RoNW showed a recovery trajectory in the terminal quarters, stabilized by capital reduction via forfeiture and cost containment.|Headwinds flagged: intense competition, volatility in raw material prices (polymers/metals), and dependence on heavy industrial cycles for moulding orders.|The proposed bullion and retail business is stated to be exposed to precious-metal price fluctuations, regulatory and compliance requirements, competition, changing consumer preferences, and inventory-management risk.

risks.risk: Management transition and change of control
risks.note: The MD&A lists this first under Risks and Concerns: 'Navigating a significant change in control and stabilizing operations post-promoter exit.' Control has passed via a Share Purchase Agreement and Open Offer by Aspect Global Ventures Private Limited, with a fresh board reconstitution and strategic redirection - so continuity of operations, customers and management depends on an incoming team, and HR effort in the second half of the year was spent on organisational restructuring to align with incoming promoter guidelines.

Flagged by management as the second Risk and Concern: several shareholders did not pay the first and final call money, and 99,01,931 partly paid-up equity shares were forfeited and cancelled. The rights-issue proceeds the Company expected therefore did not fully arrive, and management states that 'managing liquid cash flows for expansions remains a key priority.'

risks.risk: Collapse in core-business revenue and sub-scale operations
risks.note: Revenue from operations fell to approximately Rs.1.56 Crore for FY26 from Rs.5.01 Crore in FY24-25 on lower business volumes and subdued demand, and the Company recorded a net loss for the second consecutive year. Management explicitly states it 'does not presently envisage significant opportunities in its existing business segments', which makes the existing toolroom and appliance operations a shrinking base rather than a platform.

risks.risk: Execution risk in an unrelated diversification into bullion and retail
risks.note: The proposed pivot into trading and retail of gold, silver and other precious metals is contingent on shareholder approval and regulatory compliance, and the MD&A itself lists its exposures: 'fluctuations in precious metal prices, regulatory and compliance requirements, intense market competition, changing consumer preferences, and risks associated with market volatility and inventory management.' It is a working-capital-heavy business unrelated to the Company's manufacturing skill base.

risks.risk: Input-cost volatility and cyclical demand in the toolroom/moulding business
risks.note: Threats named in the MD&A: 'Intense market competition, volatility in raw material prices (polymers/metals), and dependencies on heavy industrial cycles for moulding orders.' The industry commentary adds that the toolroom and industrial core moulding segment faces heightened cost pressures and competitive pricing, and that manufacturers must optimise material costs and capacity utilisation to maintain margins.

risks.risk: Very small operating base and key-person dependence
risks.note: As of 31st March 2026 the Company employed only 6 employees other than the Directors across manufacturing, quality control, sales and marketing. Internal controls are described as 'tailored to its current scale of operations', so both operating capacity and the control environment rest on a handful of people.

risks.risk: Compliance and disclosure gaps flagged by the Secretarial Auditor
risks.note: The MR-3 report qualifies its opinion with three observations: the Promoters' shareholding is not 100% in dematerialised form; certain statutory information uploads are pending on the Company's website; and the Acquirers filed their Regulation 29(2) takeover-code disclosures on the rights-issue allotment a few days beyond the two-working-day statutory timeline. The Board's Report separately notes that Secretarial Standards SS-1 and SS-2 were complied with 'however, improvements in certain areas are being made.'

risks.risk: Unresolved promoter-group reclassification with untraceable promoters
risks.note: The Company had to partially withdraw its Regulation 31A reclassification application in respect of eight untraceable individuals because it could not produce their individual consent letters, and proceeded only with ELCOT. Those individuals remain in the Promoter/Promoter Group category, leaving the promoter register unresolved after the change in control.
